newsitem.title: EGYPT: French envoy meets Egyptian president.
newsitem.headline: French envoy meets Egyptian president.

text.p: A special envoy from French President Jacques Chirac met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo on Sunday at the start of a regional tour to prepare for Chirac's own Middle East visit, which starts on Saturday.
Envoy Bertrand Dufourcq, who is also secretary general of the foreign ministry, will be in Israel on Monday and in the Palestinian territories on Tuesday, officials said.

He told reporters after seeing Foreign Minister Amr Moussa on Saturday that Chirac wanted to consult Middle East leaders on "steps that could be taken to help move the peace process forward and ensure the current negotiations fulfil hopes".

Chirac's tour comes at a time when Arab leaders are looking to Europe to balance the perceived pro-Israeli bias of U.S. President Bill Clinton, campaigning for re-election at a time of heightened tension in the region.
The European Union has promised to appoint its own special envoy to Middle East peace talks, with a role similar to that of U.S. special coordinator Dennis Ross.
Mubarak told reporters on Saturday he welcomed a European role but it should be coordinated with the United States, which has traditionally dominated the mediation role.
"We don't want conflicts to happen and the loser to be the cause (of peace)," he said. "Europe has a role but this does not dispense with the U.S. role, because that is fundamental."
